sources.title: Halo
sources.finding: ACE lists the kettlebell Halo as Advanced and specifies a controlled path from chest over each shoulder and around/behind the head.

sources.title: How to Do the Kettlebell Halo
sources.finding: Describes halo as shoulder mobility/control work with braced core, smooth controlled circular motion and still head.

sources.title: Kettlebell High Pull: Form, Muscles & Cardio Benefits
sources.finding: Calls the high pull a fast technical exercise between one-handed swing and snatch; timing, coordination, grip and control are explicit demands.

sources.title: Kettlebell Workouts: The Ultimate Full-Body Training Guide
sources.finding: High pull links lower-body power with upper-body speed and may improve coordination for explosive lifts; execution requires hinge, hip drive and controlled close bell path.

sources.title: Double-Kettlebell Push Press and Jerk
sources.finding: Jerk adds a drop-under/rebend after explosive hip drive, catches overhead with locked elbows and is described as a demanding full-body strength and coordination challenge.

sources.title: Kettlebell Jerk 101
sources.finding: Describes kettlebell jerk as an advanced ballistic skill; timing is a key learning difficulty and limited shoulder/thoracic mobility is explicitly identified as a limiter.

sources.title: Lateral Lunge
sources.finding: ACE rates the loaded lateral lunge Intermediate and specifies lateral stepping, hip-back mechanics and controlled return.

sources.title: Side Lunge
sources.finding: ACE details balance assistance, frontal-plane weight shift, flat heels, hip flexion and knee/foot alignment through the lateral lunge.

sources.title: One-arm kettlebell press
sources.finding: NSCA technique requires overhead shoulder flexion/elbow extension with shoulder rotation, neutral spine, no lateral flexion and controlled lowering.

sources.title: How to do a Kettlebell Overhead Press
sources.finding: NASM cues core stabilization, avoidance of lumbar arch/head protrusion and full overhead arm extension.

sources.title: The Push Press
sources.finding: CrossFit states great coordination is required in the dip-drive-to-arm handoff, accuracy in vertical torso/bar path, rapid turnaround/agility and balance under overhead load.

sources.title: Double-Kettlebell Push Press and Jerk
sources.finding: Kettlebell push press uses a controlled dip, explosive leg/hip drive and overhead arm extension while maintaining upright rack mechanics.

sources.title: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
sources.finding: Exercise-specific tutorial requires rack position, long backward step, both knees bending, upright torso, strong abs, controlled heel-driven return and alternating sides.

sources.title: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge: Strength, Balance, and Joint-Friendly Power
sources.finding: Describes the kettlebell reverse lunge as unilateral lower-body strength work that improves single-leg control and uses goblet/racked loading.

sources.title: Kettlebell Lunge and Press: Build Strength, Balance and Control
sources.finding: Exercise combines reverse lunge and one-arm overhead press and is described as highly demanding in execution, challenging stability, posture, strength, balance, mobility and total-body coordination.

sources.title: Reverse Lunge to Press
sources.finding: Kettlebell demonstration identifies the exercise as unilateral, core/balance demanding and recommends prior comfort with lunges and unilateral shoulder press; balance is explicitly key.
